claims.text: 'I would like to enter into the testimony a letter I sent to the DOD regarding the case of Major David Charles Grusch, a UAP whistleblower who has been extremely helpful to this Committee. Unfortunately, due to his participation in the disclosure of UAP, he suffered reprisal like the removal of his clearance, denial of promotion, and loss of medical retirement. I wrote the DOD on July 24, 2025, on behalf of Major Grusch, and I am still waiting for a reply.'

label: Elijah Crane
narrative: Crane produced the single most specific piece of documented retaliation evidence in the House record. A former Navy SEAL, he sits on the Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets and cosponsored Burchett's H.R. 5060. On 24 July 2025 he wrote the Department of Defense on behalf of Major David Charles Grusch, and on 9 September 2025 he entered that letter into the hearing record while stating that he was still waiting for a reply. His description of what happened to Grusch is the operative fact: 'due to his participation in the disclosure of UAP, he suffered reprisal like the removal of his clearance, denial of promotion, and loss of medical retirement.' That is three discrete adverse actions against the government's own credible-and-urgent whistleblower, stated by a sitting member on a hearing record, with a letter to the Department unanswered for six weeks and counting. Crane also told the witnesses at that hearing that he had grown up thinking the subject was 'a little kooky' and had become a believer after hearing servicemembers testify and seeing the Yemen footage Burlison played.
